newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Jan-Oct current account gap 2.89 pct/GDP.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Jan-Oct current account gap 2.89 pct/GDP.

text.p: Brazil's January-October current account deficit stood at $17.233 billion, or 2.89 percent of gross domestic product, up from 2.53 percent of GDP in the January-September period, the Central Bank said.
The bank said in a statement that the 1996 result was higher than the 2.7 percent/GDP current account gap in the same period in 1995.
The bank said that net foreign reserves in October stood at $57.325 billion, or $58.6 billion according to the international liquidity concept, which includes accounts receivable.
In September net foreign reserves were $57.381 billion, or $58.775 billion, respectively.
The bank said that net foreign direct investment in October was $820 million, bringing foreign direct investment for the year so far to $6.638 billion.
The January-September foreign direct investment covered 43 percent of the current account gap, it said.
For the January-October period, fdi covered 38.5 percent of the current account deficit, the bank said.

In the balance of payments, net services showed a deficit of $16.846 billion, including $8.268 billion in interest payments. Unilateral transfers showed a surplus of $2.513 billion, compared with $3.376 billion in the same year-ago period.
